title: Giant, Fruit-Eating Bats Are Shrinking - Nautilus
gist: A Journal of Mammalogy study finds the Madagascan flying fox, a key long-distance pollinator, is physically shrinking over time, based on comparisons between field observations and Field Museum specimens.

insights.claim: A study in the Journal of Mammalogy reports that Madagascan flying foxes (Pteropus rufus) are physically shrinking over time, after field biologists noticed live bats looked smaller than specimens in the Field Museum's collections in Chicago.
insights.so_what: Body-size decline in a keystone pollinator is an early ecological-stress signal with possible knock-on effects for plant reproduction.
insights.quote: Madagascan flying foxes are physically shrinking over time
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: The Madagascan flying fox, with a wingspan up to 5 feet and foraging trips of up to 30 miles, is a key pollinator that spreads pollen widely across Madagascar.
insights.so_what: Smaller bats may mean reduced pollination services, per the article's framing of 'smaller pollinators'.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
